status_corrections.actual_source_outcome: The Definition explicitly includes K=0 and returns the readout of the embedded initial-label multiset with no layer update. At positive finite K, initialization is round0 and the final readout uses the completed roundK states.

For the supplied label-preserving vertex bijection, the defining adjacency biconditional sends each edge {u,v} of G to the edge {phi(u),phi(v)} of H. This is its explicit forward adjacency-preservation requirement.

The reverse clause of the same defining biconditional requires an image edge {phi(u),phi(v)} in H to come from {u,v} in G. Bijectivity and label preservation are simultaneous requirements, so nonedges cannot be silently collapsed.

Depth K is nonnegative. With K=0 there are no epsilon parameters or M_k updates, h_v^0 is the initial embedding, and the defined readout acts on those initial features. The positive-depth formula is applied only for1<=k<=K.

The depth K may be zero. Then the neighbor/update recursion has no layers and the graph output is R applied to the initial embedded-label multiset, using H_K=H_0. Positive depths read the state after the final prescribed layer.

The explicit list convention includes n=0: it denotes the empty multiset, whose multiplicity function is identically zero and whose support sum has size zero. Nonempty lists retain every occurrence through their index count.
The Definition states equality exactly when multiplicity functions agree. Equal multisets are the same function m:X->N_0, so evaluation at each x gives the same multiplicity.

Conversely, if all multiplicities agree at every x in X, the two multiplicity functions are equal as functions and hence are the same finite multiset. The finite-support requirement remains in force for both inputs.

At round t=0 the colors are exactly the given labels and the graph multiset is their label histogram. The tuple update starts afterward and is defined for every finite successor; the Definition does not require a last or infinite round.

The smallest admitted nonempty multiset here is the singleton S_1={x}. Verification step 2.1 divides its sum by size1 and takes a singleton coordinate maximum, both yielding x; the two-copy multiset gives the same outputs. Empty means/maxima are excluded by the stated nonempty input condition.

Verification step 1.2 starts at round0 with six copies of the common label in each graph and propagates that equality to every finite successor. There is no terminal-round assumption or limit step in this indistinguishability witness.

The bound M=0 is expressly allowed. Proof step 1.1 then has only the empty neighbor multiset and its sum code is injective; the center/pair argument in step 2.1 still uses the nonzero irrational coefficient and injective base powers.

Proof step 1.1 begins at t=0 with label preservation and extends along the vertex isomorphism to each finite round. The histogram argument in step 2.1 uses the same bijection, including the initial round, with no separate limiting endpoint.

Both-empty graphs do not meet the WL-distinction hypothesis, but one empty and one nonempty graph can meet it already at round0; their state multisets remain different under the injective maps in proof steps 1.1–2.1. Empty neighbor multisets and size bounds Delta=0 or N=0 are separately covered by the bounded-multiset construction invoked in step 3.1.

If K=0 already distinguishes the initial label histograms, the base embedding in proof step 1.1 is injective on occurring labels. Step2.1 then sends the different initial histograms to different state multisets and the injective readout separates them, without requiring a layer update.

For K=0, proof step 1.1 uses the shared initial embedding and step 2.1 applies the shared readout to equal initial-label state multisets. Thus the zero-layer endpoint is included, while every larger finite K follows the same induction.
